comply-in.span: LangChain, LangGraph, and LlamaIndex, used for what each is actually built for in 2026 production systems.
A specific framework choice, with the reasoning and measured overhead, before any build begins.
LlamaIndex retrieval wrapped as a tool inside a LangGraph agent — the standard 2026 pattern that minimizes memory and latency overhead.
If your project doesn’t need multi-step agent graphs or hierarchical indexing, I’ll say so straight away.

sec-head.h2: What is LangChain? What is LlamaIndex?

p: LangChain is a broad LLM application framework built around composable chains, agents, tools, and memory, with LangGraph as its production agent orchestration layer. LlamaIndex is a focused data framework for LLMs, purpose-built for ingesting, indexing, and querying document corpora via retrieval-augmented generation. Both are open-source, MIT-licensed, and by 2026 both frameworks handle RAG and agents to some degree — the real choice is about where your project’s hardest problem actually lives: agentic control flow or retrieval quality.

td: Multi-step agent orchestration with state, tools, and memory in LangGraph
Hierarchical index retrieval speed and query synthesis quality
Agentic systems where RAG is one component, requiring dynamic decision chains
Retrieval-first products where document Q&A is the core, with minimal agent overhead
30 to 40% less code for a comparable retrieval pipeline
500+ integrations, most mature agent tooling, LangSmith observability
300+ connectors, native document parsing via LlamaParse, lower integration complexity
LangSmith (first-party, paid tiers) with full trace and latency breakdown
Typically requires third-party tracing; LlamaTrace introduced in 2026 for basic monitoring

p: Most production systems use both together: LlamaIndex handling ingestion, hierarchical indexing, and retrieval, with LangGraph orchestrating the broader multi-step agent logic around it. This hybrid architecture delivers retrieval latency under 50ms and agent overhead under 150ms per turn — the standard I build when a project genuinely needs both retrieval quality and agentic behavior.
